First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \text{ }\,(1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta )}{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \,{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }={sec}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$
